alt: Graphs of y = 8 - x^2 and the line y = 2x meeting at (-4, -8) and (2, 4): the parabola is above the line between them, and the shaded region has area 36 square units, found by integrating upper minus lower.
caption: Figure: the area between the curves from x = −4 to x = 2 is 36 square units

alt: Argand diagram of the roots 3 + 2i and 3 - 2i of z^2 - 6z + 13 = 0: they are mirror images of each other in the real axis, so complex roots of a real quadratic form a conjugate pair with the same real part 3.
caption: Figure: the roots 3 ± 2i are reflections of each other in the real axis

alt: Argand diagram showing z = 2 - 3i, w = 1 + 4i and their sum z + w = 3 + i: the sum is the fourth vertex of the parallelogram formed by the arrows from the origin to z and to w, so real parts add (2 + 1 = 3) and imaginary parts add (-3 + 4 = 1).
caption: Figure: adding complex numbers is vector addition on the Argand diagram

alt: Smooth bend banked at 12 degrees, radius 80 m: the normal reaction R leans towards the centre; its vertical component R cos 12° balances the weight mg and its horizontal component R sin 12° supplies the central force, so tan 12° = v²/(rg) and v = 12.9 m/s.
caption: Figure: on a banked track the normal reaction supplies the central force

alt: Uniform beam AB of length 6 m resting on supports at C (1 m from A) and D (4.5 m from A) with its weight 392 N at the midpoint and a 245 N load at B: taking moments about C gives the reaction at D as 574 N, and resolving vertically gives the reaction at C as 63 N.
caption: Figure: forces on the beam: R_C = 63 N, R_D = 574 N, weight 392 N and load 245 N

alt: Bar chart of the binomial distribution B(12, 0.3): probabilities rise to a peak at X = 3 (0.240), the three bars for X = 2, 3 and 4 (0.168, 0.240, 0.231) are highlighted and sum to P(2 ≤ X ≤ 4) = 0.639, and the distribution is skewed to the right.
caption: Figure: B(12, 0.3) peaks at 3; the highlighted bars X = 2, 3, 4 give P(2 ≤ X ≤ 4) = 0.639

alt: Bar chart of the binomial distribution B(60, 0.4) with the normal curve N(24, 14.4) drawn over it: the curve follows the bar tops closely, and P(X ≥ 30) is the area of the bars from X = 30, which the normal curve approximates by the area to the right of 29.5 (the continuity correction); exact 0.0746, normal 0.0736.
caption: Figure: the bars are the binomial probabilities, the curve is N(24, 14.4); the tail from 29.5 gives P(X ≥ 30)

alt: Box-and-whisker plot of 11 daily airtime sales: minimum 9, lower quartile 9, median 15, upper quartile 22 and maximum 31 dollars, so the interquartile range is 13; the mean 16.6 (marked with a cross) is slightly above the median, and the dots below show the 11 values with three days at 9.
caption: Figure: the box spans Q₁ = 9 to Q₃ = 22 (IQR 13) with the median at 15 and whiskers to 9 and 31

alt: Box-and-whisker plot of the rainy days at 11 weather stations: the box runs from Q1 = 6 to Q3 = 11 with the median at 8, the whiskers reach 3 and 12, and the value 29, above the upper fence 18.5, is marked as an outlier with a cross.
caption: Figure: box plot with the outlier 29 beyond the upper fence 18.5

alt: Distance-time graphs for a car accelerating from rest at 2 m/s² (s = t², a curve) and a truck at constant 15 m/s (s = 15t, a straight line): the truck is ahead at first and the car overtakes it where the graphs meet, at t = 15 s and 225 m from the robot.
caption: Figure: the car overtakes the truck where the curve s = t² meets the line s = 15t, at t = 15 s

alt: Curve y = x³ + 2x with P (1, 3): the chord to Q at x = 2 (h = 1) has gradient 5 + 3 + 1 = 9, the chord to Q at x = 1.5 (h = 0.5) has gradient 5 + 1.5 + 0.25 = 6.75, and as Q moves towards P the chord gradient 5 + 3h + h² tends to 5, the gradient of the tangent at P.
caption: Figure: as h gets smaller the chord PQ turns into the tangent at P, with gradient 5 + 3h + h² → 5

alt: Circle with centre C(3, -1) and radius 5 through A(-1, 2), B(7, 2) and (6, -5), with the tangent 3x + 4y = 30 touching it at P(6, 3): the radius CP has gradient 4/3 and the tangent, perpendicular to it, has gradient -3/4.
caption: Figure: the tangent at P(6, 3) is perpendicular to the radius CP

alt: Graph of y = 2x² - 12x + 7 = 2(x - 3)² - 11: a U-shaped parabola with minimum (vertex) at (3, -11), line of symmetry x = 3, y-intercept 7 and x-intercepts 0.65 and 5.35.
caption: Figure: completing the square gives the vertex (3, −11) and the line of symmetry x = 3

alt: Unit circle with a ray at angle A (sin A = 3/5, cos A = 4/5, A = 36.9 degrees) and a ray at A + B where B adds 67.4 degrees: the point at A + B is (−16/65, 63/65), so cos(A + B) = −16/65 is negative (A + B is obtuse, 104.3 degrees) and sin(A + B) = 63/65.
caption: Figure: the coordinates of the point at angle A + B are (cos(A + B), sin(A + B)) = (−16/65, 63/65)

alt: Conical pendulum, string 0.8 m at 30 degrees to the vertical, radius 0.4 m, mass 0.3 kg: the vertical component of the tension balances the weight 2.94 N, giving T = 3.39 N, and the horizontal component 1.70 N towards the centre of the circle gives omega² = 14.1.
caption: Figure: the horizontal component of the tension is the force towards the centre; the vertical component balances the weight

alt: Graph of the temperature of a cup of tea, theta = 20 + 75e^(-0.04t): it starts at 95 degrees C, falls to 50 degrees C after 22.9 minutes and levels off towards the room temperature of 20 degrees C, which is the horizontal asymptote.
caption: Figure: θ = 20 + 75e^(−0.04t) falls from 95 °C towards the asymptote 20 °C

alt: Graph of y = cosec x for 0 to 360 degrees drawn from the dashed sine curve: vertical asymptotes at x = 0, 180 and 360 degrees where sin x = 0, a minimum point (90, 1) and a maximum point (270, -1), so cosec x never lies between -1 and 1.
caption: Figure: y = cosec x has asymptotes where sin x = 0 and turning points (90°, 1) and (270°, −1)

alt: A uniform crate 0.4 m wide and 1.2 m tall on a plank: it topples when the vertical through its centre of mass G passes through the lower edge, at tan θ = 0.2/0.6, θ = 18.4 degrees, before it would slide at 26.6 degrees (mu = 0.5).
caption: Figure: toppling starts when the vertical through G reaches the lower edge of the base

alt: Two copies of the distribution of the sample mean N(75, 1.2²): in the one-tailed test the critical region is x̄ > 76.97, in the two-tailed test it is x̄ < 72.65 or x̄ > 77.35; a sample mean of 77.1 (red line) falls in the one-tailed region but not in the two-tailed regions.
caption: Figure: the same sample mean 77.1 is significant in the one-tailed test but not in the two-tailed test

alt: Graph of y = (x + 2)(x - 1)(x - 3), a cubic with a positive x^3 coefficient: it crosses the x-axis at -2, 1 and 3 and the y-axis at (0, 6), rising from bottom left to a maximum, falling to a minimum between 1 and 3 and rising again; it is above the axis for -2 < x < 1 and for x > 3.
caption: Figure: the cubic crosses the x-axis at −2, 1 and 3 and the y-axis at (0, 6)

alt: Graph of y = x^3 - 6x^2 + 9x + 1 with its maximum (1, 5) and minimum (3, 1): a horizontal line y = k cuts the curve three times when k lies between 1 and 5, shown here for k = 3 at x = 0.27, 2 and 3.73.
caption: Figure: y = k meets the cubic three times when 1 < k < 5 (shown for k = 3)

alt: Cumulative frequency graph of the masses of 120 goats through the points (10, 0), (20, 9), (30, 36), (40, 78), (50, 108) and (70, 120): reading across from 30, 60 and 90 gives the lower quartile 27.8 kg, the median 35.7 kg and the upper quartile 44.0 kg.
caption: Figure: reading across from 30, 60 and 90 on the cumulative frequency graph gives Q₁, the median and Q₃

alt: Graph of y = 0.8^n with the line y = 0.1: the curve crosses the line at n = 10.31…, so 0.8^10 = 0.107 is still above 0.1 and 0.8^11 = 0.0859 is below, giving least integer n = 11.
caption: Figure: the decay curve y = 0.8ⁿ crosses y = 0.1 at n = 10.31, so the least whole n is 11

alt: Probability tree for three machines A, B, C making 50%, 30% and 20% of bolts with defect rates 0.02, 0.03 and 0.05: the defective branches have probabilities 0.010, 0.009 and 0.010 which total P(D) = 0.029, so P(C | D) = 0.010 ÷ 0.029 = 0.345.
caption: Figure: add the three D branches to get P(D) = 0.029; the share of machine C is 0.010 ÷ 0.029

alt: Displacement-time graph of s = t³ − 6t² + 9t + 2: the particle starts at s = 2, is at rest (turning) at t = 1 with s = 6 and at t = 3 with s = 2, and reaches s = 6 at t = 4; each of the three stages is 4 m, so the distance is 12 m but the displacement is 4 m.
caption: Figure: the turning points t = 1 and t = 3 show why distance (12 m) is more than displacement (4 m)

alt: Left, a particle of weight 20 N held by two strings at 30 and 50 degrees to the horizontal with tensions T1 = 13.1 N and T2 = 17.6 N; right, the same three forces drawn nose to tail form a closed triangle, which shows they are in equilibrium.
caption: Figure: three forces in equilibrium form a closed triangle when drawn nose to tail

alt: Graphs of y = e^x through (0, 1) with asymptote y = 0, and y = ln x through (1, 0) with asymptote x = 0: they are reflections of each other in the dashed line y = x.
caption: Figure: y = eˣ and y = ln x are reflections in y = x

alt: Exponential density f(t) = 0.25e^(-0.25t) for a battery lifetime with mean 4 years: the curve falls steadily, the median 2.77 years lies left of the mean 4, and the shaded tail from t = 6 has area e^(-1.5) = 0.223.
caption: Figure: the median (2.77 years) is below the mean (4 years) because the long right tail pulls the mean up

alt: Forces on a 3 kg block at rest on a rough plane inclined at 20 degrees: weight 30 N vertically down, normal reaction R = 28.19 N perpendicular to the plane and friction F = 10.26 N up the plane, which is less than the greatest friction available, 12.69 N.
caption: Figure: friction (10.26 N) acts up the plane and balances the component of weight down the plane

alt: Graph of y = 3 cos t + 2 sin t = sqrt(13) cos(t - 33.69 degrees) for 0 to 360 degrees: a cosine wave of amplitude sqrt(13), about 3.61, with its maximum at 33.69 degrees; the line y = 1 meets it at 107.6 and 319.8 degrees, the two solutions of 3 cos t + 2 sin t = 1.
caption: Figure: the wave √13 cos(θ − 33.69°) meets y = 1 at 107.6° and 319.8°

alt: Head-on collision on a smooth line: P (2 kg) moves right at 4 m/s and Q (3 kg) moves left at 2 m/s; momentum before is 2(4) + 3(-2) = 2 N s, and after the collision P moves left at 1 m/s so Q moves right at 4/3 = 1.33 m/s.
caption: Figure: conservation of momentum gives Q's velocity after the collision: 4/3 m/s in P's original direction

alt: Histogram of the homework times of 80 learners with unequal classes: the bar heights are frequency densities 0.8, 1.4, 1.5, 0.9 and 0.25 for the classes 0-10, 10-20, 20-40, 40-60 and 60-100 minutes, and the area of each bar equals its frequency 8, 14, 30, 18 and 10; the 20 to 40 class is the modal class.
caption: Figure: bar height is frequency density, so the area of each bar is its frequency

alt: Graphs of y = x^2 and y = 2 + e^(-x) for x from 0 to 2.6: they cross once for x > 0 at x = alpha, about 1.492, between 1 and 2; the parabola is below the exponential curve before alpha and above it afterwards.
caption: Figure: y = x² and y = 2 + e⁻ˣ meet at x = α ≈ 1.492, between 1 and 2

alt: Graphs of f(x) = (x - 2)^2 + 5 for x >= 2, starting at (2, 5), and its inverse f^-1(x) = 2 + sqrt(x - 5) starting at (5, 2): the two curves are mirror images in the dashed line y = x.
caption: Figure: f starts at (2, 5), f⁻¹ at (5, 2); each is the reflection of the other in y = x

alt: Graphs of y = x (dashed) and y = cube root of (3x + 5) with the iteration staircase starting at x1 = 2: the steps go up to the curve and across to the line, giving x2 = 2.2240, x3 = 2.2684 and so on, closing in on the intersection at x = 2.279, the root.
caption: Figure: the iteration x(n+1) = ∛(3xn + 5) climbs a staircase to the root 2.28

alt: Forces on a 5 m ladder of weight 200 N at 60 degrees against a smooth wall with a 700 N painter 4 m up it: at the foot the normal reaction R = 900 N upwards and friction F = 381 N towards the wall, and at the top the wall reaction S = 381 N horizontally away from the wall.
caption: Figure: R = 900 N and F = S = 381 N; moments about the foot give S

alt: L-shaped lamina: a 12 cm by 8 cm rectangle OABC with a 4 cm square removed at corner B has its centre of mass G at (5.2, 3.6) cm, below and left of the whole rectangle's centre (6, 4); hung from O, OG is vertical and OA makes 34.7 degrees with it.
caption: Figure: removing the corner square moves the centre of mass from (6, 4) to G (5.2, 3.6)

alt: The curve y = x² - 3x + 6 with three lines y = x + k: k = 4 cuts it at two points (discriminant 8 > 0), k = 2 touches it at (2, 4) (discriminant 0, tangent), and k = 0 misses it (discriminant -8 < 0).
caption: Figure: the sign of the discriminant 4k − 8 decides whether the line cuts, touches or misses the curve

alt: Straight-line graph of ln y against ln x through (0.5, 2.1) and (2.0, 4.8): the gradient 2.7 ÷ 1.5 = 1.8 is the power n and the intercept 1.2 on the ln y axis is ln k, so y = kx^n with n = 1.8 and k = e^1.2 = 3.32.
caption: Figure: for y = kxⁿ, a graph of ln y against ln x is a line with gradient n and intercept ln k

alt: Straight-line graph of ln y against x through (1, 3.2) and (5, 4.4): the gradient 1.2 ÷ 4 = 0.3 is ln a and the intercept 2.9 is ln k, so y = ka^x with a = e^0.3 = 1.35 and k = e^2.9 = 18.2.
caption: Figure: for y = kaˣ, a graph of ln y against x is a line with gradient ln a and intercept ln k

alt: Argand diagram of the disc |z + 3 - 4i| <= 1, centre -3 + 4i radius 1, with the line from the origin through the centre of length 5: the point of the disc nearest the origin has |z| = 4 and the farthest has |z| = 6, and the two tangents from the origin touch the circle where arg z is greatest (2.42 radians) and least (2.01 radians).
caption: Figure: the disc, the nearest and farthest points from O, and the two tangents from O

alt: Argand diagram with the points 2i and -4 joined by a dashed segment and the locus |z - 2i| = |z + 4|, the perpendicular bisector y = -2x - 3, passing through the midpoint (-2, 1): every point on this line is equally far from 2i and from -4.
caption: Figure: points equidistant from 2i and −4 lie on the perpendicular bisector y = −2x − 3

alt: Graph of y = |x^2 - 4x|: the dashed part of y = x^2 - 4x below the x-axis (vertex (2, -4)) is reflected to give a maximum at (2, 4), so the graph is W-shaped touching the axis at (0, 0) and (4, 0); the line y = 3 meets it at four points, so |x^2 - 4x| = 3 has four solutions.
caption: Figure: reflecting the dashed part in the x-axis gives a W shape; y = 3 cuts it four times

alt: Graphs of the V-shaped y = |2x - 1| with vertex (1/2, 0) and the line y = x + 4: they meet at (-1, 3) and (5, 9), and the V lies below the line between x = -1 and x = 5, so |2x - 1| < x + 4 for -1 < x < 5.
caption: Figure: the V lies below the line between the intersections, so −1 < x < 5

alt: Graph of y = x^3 - 2x - 5 near its root: the tangent at x1 = 2 (gradient 10) meets the x-axis at x2 = 2.1, and the tangent at x2 meets it at x3 = 2.0946, very close to the root 2.0946.
caption: Figure: each tangent meets the x-axis closer to the root: 2, 2.1, 2.0946

alt: Normal curve for heights X ~ N(165, 64) with the area between 153 cm (z = -1.5) and 171 cm (z = 0.75) shaded: the shaded area is the probability 0.7066.
caption: Figure: P(153 < X < 171) is the shaded area, 0.7066

alt: Normal curve for can volumes X ~ N(330, 2.5 squared) with the lower tail below 326 ml (z = -1.6) shaded: this is the probability that a can is underweight, 0.0548.
caption: Figure: the shaded lower tail, P(X < 326) = 0.0548

alt: The ellipse x = 3 cos theta, y = 2 sin theta, with x-intercepts at plus and minus 3 and y-intercepts at plus and minus 2: at theta = pi/4 the point is (2.12, 1.41) and the tangent has gradient -2/3.
caption: Figure: the ellipse x²/9 + y²/4 = 1 and its tangent at θ = π/4, gradient −2/3

alt: Partial variation C = 21 + 0.4d for a kombi hire: a straight line with intercept 21 (the fixed charge) and gradient 0.4 US dollars per km through (60, 45) and (130, 73); a 200 km trip costs US$101.
caption: Figure: partial variation is a straight line: the intercept 21 is the fixed part, the gradient 0.4 the part that varies with distance

alt: Pascal's triangle for rows 0 to 7, each entry the sum of the two above it, with row 4 (1, 4, 6, 4, 1) highlighted: these are the coefficients used to expand (2 + x)⁴ = 16 + 32x + 24x² + 8x³ + x⁴, and row 7 is 1, 7, 21, 35, 35, 21, 7, 1.
caption: Figure: row n of Pascal's triangle gives the coefficients of (a + b)ⁿ; row 4 expands (2 + x)⁴

alt: Paths of two particles on an x-y plane: P moves from (1, 5) with velocity (3, 1) and Q from (13, -5) with velocity (-2, 4); the paths cross at (7, 7), but P is there at t = 2 and Q at t = 3, so they do not collide.
caption: Figure: the paths cross at (7, 7), but the particles are there at different times (t = 2 and t = 3)

alt: The perpendicular bisector of P (1, 7) and Q (7, 3): it passes through the midpoint M (4, 5) with gradient 3/2, the negative reciprocal of the gradient -2/3 of PQ, and has equation 3x - 2y - 2 = 0.
caption: Figure: the perpendicular bisector passes through the midpoint M (4, 5) at right angles to PQ

alt: Trajectory of a ball kicked at 25 metres per second at 40 degrees above the horizontal from level ground: a parabola rising to a greatest height of 13.2 m halfway along, and landing 62.8 m away after 3.28 s.
caption: Figure: the path is a parabola: greatest height 13.2 m, range 62.8 m, time of flight 3.28 s

alt: Two trajectories of water leaving a nozzle at 30 metres per second that both pass through the window at (60, 10): the flatter path at 31.7 degrees and the higher lob at 67.7 degrees, the two roots of the quadratic in tan alpha.
caption: Figure: two launch angles, 31.7° and 67.7°, reach the same point (60, 10)

alt: A 4 kg block on a rough table (friction 10 N) joined by a string over a smooth pulley to a hanging 2 kg particle (weight 20 N): both move with acceleration 5/3 m per second squared, the string tension is 16.7 N, less than the 20 N weight of the hanging particle.
caption: Figure: forces on the 4 kg block and the 2 kg particle, with the shared tension T = 16.7 N

alt: Two particles of mass 5 kg and 3 kg hanging over a smooth pulley: the heavier one accelerates downwards and the lighter one upwards, each at 2.5 m per second squared, with the same tension 37.5 N throughout the string; the weights are 50 N and 30 N.
caption: Figure: the string tension is 37.5 N on both sides; the particles have the same acceleration size, 2.5 m/s²

alt: Graph of y = 3x^2 - 5x - 2, a U-shaped parabola crossing the x-axis at x = -1/3 and x = 2: the curve is on or below the axis between these roots, so 3x^2 - 5x - 2 <= 0 gives -1/3 <= x <= 2.
caption: Figure: the parabola is on or below the x-axis between its roots, so −1/3 ≤ x ≤ 2

alt: Graph of y = x^4 - 4x^3: the curve falls through the origin with a horizontal tangent but no turning point there, a stationary point of inflexion at (0, 0), then reaches a minimum at (3, -27) and rises.
caption: Figure: y = x⁴ − 4x³ flattens at (0, 0) without turning, then has a minimum at (3, −27)

alt: Sector OAB of a circle of radius 6 cm with angle 2π/3 at O: the arc AB is 4π cm (12.57), the chord AB is 6√3 cm (10.39), and the minor segment between chord and arc has area 12π − 9√3 cm², the sector minus triangle OAB.
caption: Figure: the minor segment is the sector OAB minus triangle OAB; arc 4π cm, chord 6√3 cm

alt: Graph of y = (2x + 1)/(x - 1): a hyperbola with vertical asymptote x = 1 and horizontal asymptote y = 2; the left branch passes through (-1/2, 0) and (0, -1), and the right branch lies above y = 2.
caption: Figure: y = 2 + 3/(x − 1) has asymptotes x = 1 and y = 2

alt: Argand diagram of the three roots of z^3 = 8i: they lie on the circle of radius 2 at arguments pi/6, 5pi/6 and -pi/2, the points sqrt(3) + i, -sqrt(3) + i and -2i, which are the vertices of an equilateral triangle 120 degrees apart.
caption: Figure: the cube roots of 8i are equally spaced on the circle |z| = 2

alt: Scatter diagram of rainfall and maize yield for eight farms with the regression line y = -0.445 + 0.603x: the points lie close to the line, which passes through the mean point (6.5, 3.475) and predicts a yield of about 3.78 tonnes per hectare at x = 7.
caption: Figure: the regression line y = −0.445 + 0.603x passes through the mean point (6.5, 3.475)

alt: Graph of y = sec x for 0 to 360 degrees drawn from the dashed cosine curve: vertical asymptotes at x = 90 and 270 degrees where cos x = 0, minimum points (0, 1) and (360, 1), a maximum point (180, -1), and no values between -1 and 1.
caption: Figure: y = sec x has asymptotes where cos x = 0 and never lies between −1 and 1

alt: A shear with matrix (1 2; 0 1) maps the triangle (1, 0), (3, 0), (1, 2) to (1, 0), (3, 0), (5, 2): points on the x-axis stay fixed, the top vertex slides 4 units parallel to the axis, and both triangles have base 2 and height 2, so the area (2) is unchanged because the determinant is 1.
caption: Figure: a shear keeps the base fixed and slides the top vertex, so the area does not change

alt: Displacement-time graph of simple harmonic motion x = 0.5 sin(πt/2): a sine wave of amplitude 0.5 m and period 4 s starting at the centre O; the particle first reaches x = 0.3 m at t = 0.410 s.
caption: Figure: starting from O, SHM x = 0.5 sin(πt/2) first reaches 0.3 m after 0.410 s

alt: A particle on a rough plane inclined at 25 degrees with mu = 0.2: moving up the slope, friction F = 0.2R acts down the slope and the deceleration is 6.04 m/s²; sliding down, friction acts up the slope and the acceleration is 2.41 m/s². Friction always opposes the motion.
caption: Figure: friction acts against the motion, so the same slope gives different accelerations up and down

alt: Graphs of y = sin x, y = x and y = tan x for x from 0 to 1.2 radians: near zero all three coincide, at x = 0.5 sin x = 0.479, x = 0.5 and tan x = 0.546, and they separate as x grows, so sin x ≈ x and tan x ≈ x only for small x.
caption: Figure: sin x and tan x hug the line y = x near 0 and separate as x grows

alt: Concentric circles x^2 + y^2 = 2c centred at the origin, the family of solution curves of dy/dx = -x/y, shown for radii 1, 2 and 3; the short amber segments show the gradient -x/y at points on the circle of radius 2, each perpendicular to the radius.
caption: Figure: the solutions of dy/dx = −x/y are circles about the origin; the gradient is perpendicular to the radius

alt: Family of solution curves y = A e^(x^2/2) of dy/dx = xy for A = 0.5, 1, 2 and 3: each curve is symmetrical about the y-axis with a minimum at x = 0, and the initial condition y = 2 when x = 0 picks out the single curve y = 2 e^(x^2/2).
caption: Figure: the general solution is a family of curves; y = 2 at x = 0 selects A = 2

alt: Tension-extension graph for a string of natural length 0.8 m and modulus 24 N: a straight line of gradient λ/l = 30 N/m, so a load of 4.9 N gives extension 0.163 m and the area under the line, the stored elastic energy, is 0.40 J.
caption: Figure: the area under the tension–extension line is the elastic energy stored

alt: Graph of the surface area A = 2 pi r^2 + 256 pi / r of a closed tin of volume 128 pi cm^3 against the radius r: A falls to a minimum of 96 pi, about 302 cm^2, at r = 4 cm and rises again for larger r.
caption: Figure: the surface area of the tin is least, 96π ≈ 302 cm², when r = 4 cm

alt: Graphs of y = sin x (grey) and y = 3 sin 2x + 1 (blue) for 0 to 360 degrees: the stretch of factor 1/2 in x halves the period to 180 degrees, the stretch of factor 3 in y gives amplitude 3, and the translation up 1 puts the centre line at y = 1, so the greatest value is 4 and the least is -2.
caption: Figure: sin x becomes 3 sin 2x + 1: period 180°, amplitude 3, centre line y = 1

alt: Graph of y = ln x from x = 1 to 3 with four trapezia: because the curve is concave (bends downwards) every chord lies below it, so the trapezium estimate 1.2821 is an under-estimate of the true area 1.2958.
caption: Figure: for the concave curve y = ln x the chords lie below the curve, so the rule under-estimates

alt: Graph of y = sqrt(1 + x^3) from x = 0 to 2 divided into four strips of width 0.5: the ordinates are 1, 1.0607, 1.4142, 2.0917 and 3, and the tops of the trapezia are straight chords that lie slightly above the curve, so the trapezium rule estimate is 3.2833.
caption: Figure: four trapezia of width 0.5 under y = √(1 + x³)

alt: Tree diagram for two sweets taken without replacement from 8 orange and 4 lemon: the first-stage branches are 8/12 and 4/12; after an orange the second branches are 7/11 and 4/11, after a lemon 8/11 and 3/11; the four outcomes OO, OL, LO and LL have probabilities 56/132, 32/132, 32/132 and 12/132.
caption: Figure: multiply along each path; the second-stage probabilities change because there is no replacement

alt: Graph of y = 1 - 2 cos x for 0 to 2 pi: it starts at a minimum of -1 when x = 0, crosses the x-axis at x = pi/3, reaches a maximum of 3 at x = pi, crosses the axis again at x = 5pi/3 and returns to -1 at x = 2pi; the range is -1 to 3.
caption: Figure: y = 1 − 2cos x has range −1 ≤ y ≤ 3 and crosses the x-axis at π/3 and 5π/3

alt: Graph of y = sin 2x for 0 to 360 degrees with the horizontal line y = 0.3: the line cuts the two waves at four points, x = 8.7, 81.3, 188.7 and 261.3 degrees, so sin 2x = 0.3 has 4 solutions in this interval.
caption: Figure: the line y = 0.3 crosses y = sin 2x four times in 0° to 360°

alt: Graph of y = sin 2x for x between minus pi and pi with the line y = -1/3: the line meets the curve four times, at x = -1.40, -0.170, 1.74 and 2.97, the four solutions of 3 sin 2x + 1 = 0.
caption: Figure: the four solutions of sin 2x = −1/3 are where the line meets the curve

alt: The lines y = 2x - 1 and x + 3y = 18 meet at P (3, 5) and cut the y-axis at (0, -1) and (0, 6); the shaded triangle has base 7 on the y-axis and height 3 (the x-coordinate of P), so its area is 10.5 square units.
caption: Figure: the triangle has its base on the y-axis, so the height is the x-coordinate of P

alt: Rectangular distribution U(0, 15) for the waiting time at a kombi rank: a flat density of 1/15 between 0 and 15 minutes; the shaded area from 10 to 15 is P(W > 10) = 5/15 = 1/3, the mean is 7.5 minutes and the standard deviation is 4.33 minutes.
caption: Figure: for a rectangular distribution, probability is a rectangle's area: P(W > 10) = 5/15

alt: Triangle ABC with A (2, 0, 1), B (5, 4, 1), C (3, 1, 6): the vectors AB = 3i + 4j and AC = i + j + 5k both start at A, AB·AC = 7, |AB| = 5 and |AC| = √27, so angle BAC = 74.4 degrees.
caption: Figure: angle BAC is found from the two vectors that start at A: cos BAC = 7 ÷ (5√27)

alt: Sketch of the line l1 with direction 2i - j + k and the point P(5, 3, -1) off the line: the foot of the perpendicular F(3, 1, 1) is the point of l1 with s = 1, where PF is perpendicular to the line, and the perpendicular distance is the length of PF, root 12, about 3.46.
caption: Figure: F(3, 1, 1) is where PF meets l₁ at a right angle; the distance PF is √12

alt: Side view of the plane x + y + 2z = 15 seen edge-on and the line with direction (2, -1, 3) meeting it at (5, 0, 5): the angle phi between the line and the plane is 49.8 degrees, while the angle between the line and the normal n = (1, 1, 2) is 40.2 degrees, so sin phi, not cos, comes from the dot product.
caption: Figure: the angle with the plane (49.8°) and the angle with the normal (40.2°) add to 90°

alt: Parallelogram OABC with O the origin, A (1, 2, 4), B (4, 6, 5) and C (3, 4, 1) where OC = AB = b − a: the diagonals OB and AC both have midpoint (2, 3, 2.5), so they bisect each other.
caption: Figure: in parallelogram OABC the diagonals OB and AC meet at their common midpoint M (2, 3, 2.5)

alt: Sketch of the plane 2x - y + 2z = 3 and the point P(4, -1, 3) above it: the shortest distance is along the normal n = (2, -1, 2) to the foot F(4/3, 1/3, 1/3), and the distance PF is 4, the same as the formula gives.
caption: Figure: the shortest distance from P to the plane is along the normal, meeting the plane at F

alt: Velocity-time graph of v = 0.6t² − 0.04t³ for 0 to 15 s: the particle starts and ends at rest, its greatest speed is 20 m/s at t = 10 (where a = 0), and the shaded area under the curve, the integral from 0 to 15, is the distance 168.75 m.
caption: Figure: the area under the velocity–time curve is the distance travelled, 168.75 m

alt: Venn diagram of 30 learners: 11 take Biology only, 6 take both Biology and Chemistry, 6 take Chemistry only and 7 take neither; the Biology circle totals 17 and the Chemistry circle totals 12.
caption: Figure: fill the Venn diagram from the middle outwards: 6, then 11 and 6, then 7 outside

alt: Region between y = 9 - x^2 and the line y = 5 for x from -2 to 2, with its reflection in the x-axis: rotating about the x-axis gives a solid with a hole, with outer radius 9 - x^2 and inner radius 5, so the volume is pi times the integral of (9 - x^2)^2 minus 25.
caption: Figure: outer radius 9 − x², inner radius 5; subtract the inner solid

alt: Region under y = x^2 for 0 to 2, shown with its mirror image below the x-axis to represent the solid formed by rotating it about the x-axis: each thin slice at x is a disc of radius y = x^2, so the volume is the integral of pi y^2 dx, which is 32 pi over 5.
caption: Figure: rotating the region about the x-axis; each slice is a disc of radius x²

alt: Velocity-time graph v = 6 - 2t from (0, 6) to (5, -4), crossing the time axis at t = 3: the area above the axis is 9 m forward and the area below is 4 m backward, so the displacement is 5 m but the distance travelled is 13 m.
caption: Figure: area above the axis (9 m) minus area below (4 m) gives displacement 5 m; the sum gives distance 13 m

alt: Velocity-time graph of a train: a line from (0, 0) up to (30, 24), horizontal to (150, 24), then down to (190, 0); the areas of the two triangles and the rectangle are 360 m, 2880 m and 480 m, so the total distance is 3720 m.
caption: Figure: the area under the velocity–time graph is the distance, 3720 m
